facts: Every OCX package targets a platform, which is an OS and architecture pair, a refinement, a feature requirement, or any. [L7]
One string form serves the --platform flag, the ocx.lock per-platform digest map and the build receipt written beside a bundle. [L9]
A platform is either the literal any, or an os/arch pair optionally refined by a CPU variant and a feature list. [L16]
The first fence gives the one-line shape: os/arch, optional variant, optional plus feature list, or any. [L19]
The os set is closed to linux, darwin, windows, wasip1 and wasip2. [L27]
any means platform-agnostic, with no OS, architecture or feature requirement. [L43]
A slash introduces the variant and a single plus introduces the feature list, so the two slots cannot be confused. [L45]
A pair must name a buildable artifact, so OCX enforces an explicit list rather than the cross product. [L52]
Six native pairs are supported: linux, darwin and windows, each on amd64 and arm64. [L58]
A pairing outside the list is refused while parsing, and the refusal lists the supported pairs. [L73]
OCX percent-escapes the four structural characters wherever they appear inside a registry-controlled value. [L85]
Parsing and re-rendering a platform string always yields the identical string, an injective round trip. [L98]
A manifest published as linux/amd64+libc.musl does not match a glibc host, because the relation decides, not equality. [L107]
An any offer satisfies every requirement, because a platform-agnostic artifact runs anywhere. [L122]
An any requirement is satisfied only by an any offer, so an undetectable host never runs a Specific binary. [L124]
os.features inverts: every feature the offer declares must be among the host capabilities the requirement offers. [L127]
variant is strict equality, and an offer that leaves variant unset imposes no constraint. [L130]
A tie is reported as ambiguous with exit 65 rather than guessed, and the caller must pass --platform. [L165]
Rosetta 2 is the canonical case, letting a darwin/amd64-only build serve darwin/arm64 hosts. [L177]
The callout notes that a shared digest is not a publishing mistake, since index entries are content-addressed. [L184]
